## What this book is

The [interactive browser](https://jwomackmu.shinyapps.io/e2f-heart-scrna/) shows
*results*. It has no room to say what threshold produced a gene list, why a contrast
is phase-matched, or which of two plausible methods was chosen and what the other one
would have said. This book is that missing half: one chapter per analysis behind the
app, each stating the question, the method with its real parameters, the result, **the
reasoning behind the choice**, and what the result cannot be used to claim.

Every chapter names the app tabs it documents, so the two can be read side by side.
Every figure here was generated by the app's own plotting code, and every number in a
table was read out of the data bundle rather than typed — see
[the colophon](#how-this-book-is-made).

## The experiment

Single-cell RNA-seq of **E2F7/8 double-knockout versus wild-type mouse heart**, at
**P0** and **P7** — four libraries, one animal each, sequenced over two lanes apiece.

The assay is **PIP-seq, chemistry V** (particle-templated instant partitions — originally
Fluent BioSciences, now sold by Illumina as *Single Cell 3' RNA Prep*), **not 10x
Chromium**. Counting was done by the vendor's own pipeline, **PIPseeker v3.3.0**, aligning
with STAR 2.7.6a against Ensembl GRCm38. Those parameters are cited to the original run's
own records, now in the repository at `original_Han_analysis/`;
[chapter 1](01-upstream.qmd) documents the whole upstream stage, including two claims this
book previously got wrong.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["4 libraries<br/>WT-P0 · WT-P7<br/>KO-P0 · KO-P7"] --> B["QC<br/>≥1,500 genes<br/>≤20% mito"]
  B --> C["Doublet removal<br/>Scrublet +<br/>scDblFinder"]
  C --> D["SCTransform<br/>glmGamPoi<br/>~2,000 HVGs"]
  D --> E["Harmony<br/>over the<br/>4 libraries"]
  E --> F["Clusters + UMAP<br/>7 cell types"]
  F --> G["CM re-clustering<br/>res 0.2<br/>CM0–CM12"]
  G --> H["app_data.rds<br/>the bundle"]
  H --> I["Shiny app<br/>18 tabs"]
  H --> J["6 builders<br/>scores · axes · DE<br/>enrichment · signalling"]
  J --> H
  style H fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
  style I fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#e65100
```

The boxed step in the middle is the one boundary worth knowing before reading further.
Everything left of `app_data.rds` ran in a separate analysis workspace and is **not in
this repository**; everything right of it is here, parameterised, and re-runnable. The
[Upstream processing](01-upstream.qmd) chapter says exactly which parameters that
costs us.

## The dataset as bundled

{{< include _generated/tbl-celltypes.md >}}

Two numbers in that table deserve emphasis, because several "n" figures in the app
follow from them. The bundle is a **stratified downsample** of the upstream object, and
the genome-wide matrix inside it is downsampled **again** — 24,221 genes across 8,026
cells, against 2,181 curated genes across all 30,030. Which matrix a panel is reading
changes what it can show, and sometimes whether a contrast runs at all. That trade is
the subject of [The cell atlas](02-atlas.qmd) and reappears in
[The four-group design](07-fourgroup.qmd).

## Where each app tab is documented

The navbar has four menus: **Whole heart** (all cell types), **Cardiomyocytes** (the
compartment deep-dive), **Methods & provenance** (diagnostics and where numbers came from),
and **Help**.

| App tab | Chapter |
|---|---|
| UMAP explorer · Gene detail · Composition | [2 — The cell atlas](02-atlas.qmd) |
| DE by cell type · Subset & DEGs | [3 — Differential expression](03-de.qmd) |
| Pathways & enrichment | [4 — Pathway enrichment](04-enrichment.qmd) |
| Cardiomyocyte deep-dive | [5 — The cardiomyocyte deep-dive](05-cm-deepdive.qmd) |
| E2F focus | [6 — E2F7/8 themselves](06-e2f.qmd) |
| Four-group (WT/KO × P0/P7) | [7 — The four-group design](07-fourgroup.qmd) |
| Cell-cycle exit & ploidy · Maturation & metabolism | [8 — Module scores and gene axes](08-scores.qmd) |
| Maturation ∩ P7 KO · Gene-set Venn · WT programs ∩ KO clusters | [9 — Crossing gene sets](09-overlaps.qmd) |
| Cell–cell signalling | [10 — Cell–cell signalling](10-signalling.qmd) |
| QC & normalization · Annotation check | [1 — Upstream processing](01-upstream.qmd) |
| About / caveats | [11 — Confounds and reproducibility](11-confounds-repro.qmd) |

A script asserts this table is complete: `tools/check_docs_coverage.py` parses the
`nav_panel()` titles out of `shiny_app/app.R` and fails if any tab is undocumented, or
if a chapter claims a tab that no longer exists.

## How this book is made {#how-this-book-is-made}

Two rules, both of which exist because a methods document is exactly where prose
quietly drifts away from the data it describes.

**Every figure is the app's figure.** `docs/export_assets.R` loads the app's own
plotting functions out of `shiny_app/app.R` and calls them against the same bundle the
app reads, so `go_dotplot_gg()` in this book and in the running app are the same
function over the same data. Nothing is redrawn from a description. The handful of
panels the app builds inside server reactives — which cannot be called from outside —
are mirrored in the exporter with the `app.R` line range they mirror written next to
them. The UMAP is the one honest exception: the app draws it in WebGL, which has no
vector export, so the book shows a static plot of the same coordinates and palette.

**No number here is typed by hand.** Load-bearing tables are generated fragments; a
rebuilt bundle changes the book. Numbers that do appear inline in prose carry a
`file:line` citation to the source that sets them, so a reviewer can check the claim
against the code rather than against my memory. This is the discipline
`shiny_app/build_deck.R` already applies to the lab-meeting deck.

Rendering the book executes nothing: every chapter is `engine: markdown` and the render
image does not have R installed. See `docs/README.md` for the commands.
